correctness.rationale: The fourth Schatten trace is phase-independent for length-four words on C7, giving F_q(x)=sum x_j^2+q sum x_j x_(j+1) on the full nonnegative unit simplex and q∈[0,2]. The C7 Fourier spectrum controls global uniform strict convexity until sec(π/7), with exactly its two-dimensional kernel at equality. For larger q, a negative zero-sum mode excludes full support, the alternating sine mode excludes 6-positive paths, and explicit stationary sign obstructions exclude all 5-positive missing-edge patterns except singleton plus four-path. All size-four supports either embed in a surviving five-face (28/35) or form exceptional two disjoint edges (7/35), whose lower bound is strictly worse; size≤3 has F≥1/3. The five-face Hessian changes sign at sec(π/5)=sqrt5−1, yielding a positive five-supported stationary point below threshold, an exact nonnegative 1D segment at threshold, and then a unique four-supported edge-plus-isolates profile. At q=2 the energy is 1/3 with exactly the stated seven boundary segments. Rational symbolic sign factorizations verify all candidate comparisons; phase freedom, norm normalization and endpoint thresholds checked. The independent checker evaluated 396 direct complex-matrix identities, all 127 nonempty supports at each of 15 interior q values using support-wise stationary/KKT/tangent-Hessian tests, all 35 four-support graph patterns, 225 q1 Fourier points, 39 q2 critical points, and 53 q=2 endpoint segment points. Finite tests alone do not prove the all-q theorem; analytical support exhaustion supplies the global argument.
residual_risks: Only the displayed seven-cycle with Schatten exponent four, 0≤t≤1 and Frobenius squared normalization is proved; no all-cycle or other Schatten p extension.
The separate parametric numerical support scan is finite and not a proof for all real q; global correctness uses support exclusions, Hessian eigenvalue signs and exact stationary formulas.

originality.rationale: The exact seven-cycle fixed-Frobenius fourth-Schatten global minimum and complete q-dependent equality classification are not mathematically implied by the closest inspected published records. The nilpotent-shift theorem gives a maximum Rayleigh-quotient for a path under ℓ4-normalization; this is a minimum copositive simplex problem for an odd cycle under ℓ2/Frobenius normalization. Pal–Chandok gives generalized-Aluthge operator bounds rather than the seven-entry constrained minimum. Standard quadratic-programming Motzkin–Straus specializations yield at most the q=2 optimum value, not the interior cutoffs and all equality fibres. Publication priority remains qualified: unindexed cycle-specific copositivity theorems and incompletely accessed operator papers remain risks.
residual_risks: A known unpublished or poorly indexed copositive simplex-quadratic classification for C7 or odd cycles with diagonal coefficient τ≥1 could contain this result implicitly; direct theorem text not identified.

value.rationale: The result solves a natural complete extremal classification for weighted cyclic shifts of the first odd size with the additional four-path spectral threshold. It proves two distinct sharp support transitions at sec(π/7) and sec(π/5), with a genuinely nontrivial intermediate five-positive-weight phase, exact analytic optimum and all critical equality continua. Under a standard Frobenius energy constraint this is a reusable exact benchmark for Schatten-fourth radius and graph-constrained simplex quadratic optimization, not merely a generic norm inequality, routine renaming, a sampled minimum or known isolated endpoint number.
residual_risks: This is an exact natural finite-dimensional model, not a theorem for arbitrary cycles or Schatten powers. No downstream result or wider classification is claimed.
